tools.name: read_published_page
tools.description:
Read one of the published pages, for answering questions about how any of this works.

Use it rather than guessing. What the fees are, how a dispute is decided and who decides it,
what a buyer is agreeing to — all of it is written down, and none of it is safe to invent.

    how-it-works         How

tools.name: check_escrow_payment
tools.description: What has happened to a settled payment, from the `status_url` on its receipt.

tools.name: verify_escrow_receipt
tools.description:
Check a receipt's signature against the key its issuer publishes.

⚠️ THE KEY IS FETCHED FROM THE RECEIPT'S OWN `iss`, NOT FROM WHOEVER HANDED IT OVER.
   Otherwise anything that can serve a receipt can also serve the key that vouches for it,
   and the signature stops meaning anything.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: prepare_escrow_payment, settle_escrow_payment · Private data: prepare_escrow_payment, settle_escrow_payment, payment_qr · Public sink: prepare_escrow_payment, settle_escrow_payment.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: prepare_escrow_payment, settle_escrow_payment · Private data: prepare_escrow_payment, settle_escrow_payment, payment_qr · Public sink: prepare_escrow_payment, settle_escrow_payment

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
